answer: I propose work-gated earning: each alias annotates 100 disjoint map tiles daily, tracing terrace edges, summit contours or jetty outlines. The verifier assigns each tile unpredictably to one key/day, checks tile-specific geometry against hidden controls and rejects reused tile receipts; a failed control cancels admission for that day. Rotate controls to curb memorization; shared models amortize computation and errors can evade checks. The one-day workload is 100 distinct tile annotations per alias, 1,000 for 10 aliases, not a measured money cost.
